claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Dockerfile` lines 5-17 match the lesson's block character for character. Line 25 `COPY --from=build /app .` is the later use of the `AS build` name the prose mentions; line 19 is the second FROM.

"There are runtime images for production and SDK images for building your code". Measured locally: mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 = 917MB; the built donhang-api:stage-1 (aspnet:10.0 base + app) = 241MB.

Lesson now uses the R1 suggested_text. publish: "publishes the resulting set of files to a directory"; "the hosting system may or may not have the .NET shared runtime installed" (framework-dependent here, no --self-contained). restore: "uses NuGet to look for these dependencies and download them". -c Release: "optimized for production deployment". --no-restore: "Doesn't execute an implicit restore".

stage-1 global.json: {"version": "10.0.300", "rollForward": "latestFeature"}. global-json.md: rollForward is "a directive to use a later version"; latestFeature accepts later feature bands/patches. "says which SDK versions the repository accepts" matches (image SDK 10.0.401 is accepted).

stage-1 scripts/up.sh runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`, and compose.yml gives api `build: DonHang.Api/Dockerfile`, `image: donhang-api:stage-1`, so the lab start does build it. R1 run (compose v2.33.1): steps 2-11 CACHED, labels `[api build  7/11]`; step 1 printed as `#6 [api build  1/11] FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0` DONE 0.0s. Step 1 IS labelled; it is only not marked CACHED.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: scripts/up.sh, docker-compose.yml; R1 docker compose build api on a stage-1 copy
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: step 1, the `FROM` line, is reused but not marked `CACHED`.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Docs: "For the ADD and COPY instructions ... the builder calculates a cache checksum from file metadata"; "Once the cache is invalidated, all subsequent Dockerfile commands generate new images". Run: appending a comment to DonHang.Api.csproj gave steps 2-5 CACHED, `[build 6/11] COPY DonHang.Api/DonHang.Api.csproj` DONE, `[build 7/11] RUN dotnet restore` DONE 10.0s, steps 8-11 DONE.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/docker-docs/content/manuals/build/cache/invalidation.md; docker build on a stage-1 copy

claim_verdicts.evidence: Lesson now matches the R1 suggested_text (same commands, same app, runs outside a container). publish output is framework-dependent: "ready for deployment to a hosting system (for example, a server, PC, Mac, laptop)"; the runtime condition is stated in the lesson's Core concepts. No byte-identical wording remains.

".NET images are regularly updated whenever a new .NET patch is published or when an operating system base image is updated." The lesson says only that builds using the same image use the same SDK, which holds; it no longer claims every machine gets the same SDK.

"Docker already has all the layers from the first image, so it doesn't need to pull them again". A machine with none of the layers must download all of them, so "every new machine has to download all of it" holds.

cli-c-release.md: "sets the build configuration to Release, which is optimized for production deployment." cli-configuration-publish-pack.md: "The default build configuration is `Debug` for earlier versions". Dockerfile line 19: `FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final`; it is the last stage, so compose builds it and prints its steps (R1 run built donhang-api:stage-1 on aspnet:10.0).

issues.quote: step 1, the `FROM` line, is just reused and is not labelled.
issues.text: In the real output step 1 IS labelled (`[api build  1/11] FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0`, DONE 0.0s); it just lacks the `CACHED` marker. A learner who sees the label will think the text is wrong.
issues.fix: Replace with: "step 1, the `FROM` line, is reused but not marked `CACHED`." Update claim 5 to "step 1 FROM reused, not marked CACHED".

issues.quote: With the SDK version and source files you have on your own machine, the image runs the commands you would run there and builds that app
issues.text: Read literally, the image uses the SDK version you have on your machine; the next sentence says the SDK comes from the image, not the machine. The condition (same SDK version) got lost in the split.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Given the same SDK version and source files as on your own machine, the image runs the commands you would run there and builds the same app, and the output runs outside a container too."

issues.quote: Docker keeps each step's result and reuses it while that step and everything before it are unchanged, and once one step changes, every step after it runs again.
issues.text: New general rule, not in the ledger. It is true (invalidation.md:40 "Once the cache is invalidated, all subsequent Dockerfile commands generate new images"), but claim 6 covers only the csproj case.
issues.fix: Extend claim 6 text: "...; general rule: a step is reused while it and every earlier step are unchanged, and once one misses the cache every later step runs again." No lesson change.

issues.quote: The same app, because the image runs the same `dotnet` commands
issues.text: Key is still the only defensible option, but its reason drops the condition the lesson states: the same commands with a different SDK (image 10.0.401 vs a laptop's 10.0.300) need not give the same app.
issues.fix: Reword option a (en/vi): "The same app, if the SDK version and source files match, because the image runs the same `dotnet` commands".

issues.quote: Running the finished app needs much less: only the runtime, not the compiler and the build tools.
issues.text: "runtime" / ".NET runtime" is not in known_vocab and not defined in Core concepts, yet it appears in Core concepts (dotnet publish), §4 and the first misconception. I can guess it is 'the part of .NET that runs the app', but the SDK-vs-runtime contrast is exactly what the section asks me to hold on to.
issues.fix: Add one sentence in §4 (or a clause in the .NET SDK bullet): "The .NET runtime is the part of .NET that runs an already compiled app; the SDK contains the runtime plus the compiler and build tools."

issues.quote: The order of the steps is chosen for the build cache.
issues.text: "build cache" is not in known_vocab (I know 'cache' and 'image layer'), and it is not defined here. The lesson that taught it, devops.l1.dockerfile-and-layers, is only in Connections, not in prereqs or Before you start, so I get no summary of it. The main idea of the lesson rests on this term.
issues.fix: Add devops.l1.dockerfile-and-layers to prereqs and to Before you start with one line: "you know that Docker caches the result of each Dockerfile step and reuses it while that step's inputs have not changed."

issues.quote: `FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0 AS build` starts from the .NET 10 SDK image;
issues.text: "Dockerfile" and its instructions FROM, COPY, RUN are not in known_vocab and not in either prereq summary. The prose explains WORKDIR and AS build but assumes FROM/COPY/RUN. I know them only if the dockerfile-and-layers lesson taught them, which this lesson does not say.
issues.fix: Same prereq fix as for 'build cache'; in the Before you start line for devops.l1.dockerfile-and-layers, mention that it taught FROM, COPY and RUN.

issues.quote: A change to `Program.cs` changes the later copy step, so the steps before it, including the slow restore, are reused from the cache.
issues.text: §4 says the steps before a changed step are reused, but never says the other half of the rule: once a step misses the cache, every step after it runs again. Without that, I cannot see why copying the source before restore would be bad. The rule first appears in the misconceptions and the Try-it answer.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one: "The changed copy step and every step after it run again; that is why the slow restore is placed before it."

issues.quote: "The same base image should run the app in production as compiled it, since that avoids extra steps."
issues.text: "production" is not in known_vocab; I know 'deploy' but not what 'in production' means as a place. "base image" is also new wording, though I can guess it is the FROM image.
issues.fix: Replace "in production" with "when the API is deployed" and "base image" with "image in `FROM`".

issues.quote: on a clean Linux inside Docker, where nothing is installed unless the `Dockerfile` brings it.
issues.text: "Linux" is not in known_vocab, and "a clean Linux" reads as jargon. The point (an empty machine with nothing installed) is clear without it.
issues.fix: Replace "on a clean Linux inside Docker" with "inside Docker, on an empty system".

issues.quote: Expected result: 1 — steps `2/11` to `11/11` are marked `CACHED`
issues.text: On a first build I would expect everything to run, so seeing all steps CACHED surprised me. I had to guess it is because `scripts/up.sh` already built this image when the lab started.
issues.fix: Add at the start of result 1: "The lab's start already built this image, so".

issues.quote: look at the `build` steps, numbered `1/11` to `11/11`.
issues.text: The file continues with a second FROM, so the output will likely also show steps from that part. I would not know whether to count them or ignore them.
issues.fix: Add: "Ignore the steps of the second part of the file; their labels do not say `build`."

issues.text: "optimised version" implies another, non-optimised version I have never heard of. I cannot tell what Release changes or why the Dockerfile wants it.
issues.fix: Replace with "`-c Release` builds the optimised version meant for running, instead of the default one meant for debugging".

issues.quote: Nothing about the result is special to Docker: with the same SDK version and the same source files, `dotnet publish` in the image builds the same app from the same commands you would run on your own machine, and the output runs outside a container too.
issues.text: I re-read this sentence twice: 'same' appears four times and it carries three ideas (same app, same commands, runs outside a container).
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: "With the same SDK version and source files, `dotnet publish` in the image builds the same app as on your machine. The output is an ordinary .NET app and runs outside a container too."

issues.quote: It is the same app, given the same SDK version and source files
issues.text: The correct option is almost word for word §4 ("with the same SDK version and the same source files ... builds the same app"), so it can be matched without understanding.
issues.fix: Reword option a, e.g. "An ordinary .NET app that could also run on a laptop, if built by the same SDK from the same code".
